title: A review of environmental benefits supplied by Agri-Environment Schemes
description: This document describes a comprehensive evaluation of various agri-environment schemes (AES) in the UK, designed to promote sustainable land use and protect biodiversity. The schemes, including the Countryside Stewardship Scheme and others, offer management options for maintaining and restoring diverse habitats. The evaluation employs diverse methodologies, such as monitoring programs and botanical surveys, to assess the impact on biodiversity, habitats, and the historic environment. Results show that AES have generally been successful in enhancing environmental values, particularly for biodiversity, with positive effects on plant and bird populations. However, outcomes are mixed, with some areas showing significant improvements and others less so. The evaluation concludes that while AES are crucial for achieving environmental policy goals, they require better design, management, and targeted measures to improve effectiveness. It also emphasizes the importance of robust evaluation studies to inform policy and notes the potential for further improvement with increased investment and strategic development.
